messages:
fiona: Heads up — hitting a weird one on mac with the quickstart. First call fails in the sample app with a low-level TLS error, but curl later shows a billing_required body.
mohit: Any network filters or adblockers? macOS apps like 1Password or Little Snitch can install network extensions that intercept TLS. Paste the exact sample output?
fiona: From running the Swift sample in the extension: 
```
Error Domain=NSPOSIXErrorDomain Code=54 "Connection reset by peer"
NSURLSession/HTTP load failed (kCFErrorDomainCFNetwork error 1.)
```
Then when I ran curl manually I got: 
```
$ curl -v https://api.play.redwood.ai/v1/health -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY"
< HTTP/1.1 402 Payment Required
{"error":"billing_required","message":"workspace needs billing setup"}
```
So the sample app shows a generic connection reset, which made me think TLS or local extension, but the backend is actually returning billing_required.
grace: Two overlapping things likely: 1) local network extension intercepts and sometimes resets TLS which surfaces as connection reset in Apple frameworks, 2) if you then retry and reach the server you might see the billing gate. Users see the ambiguous connection error and assume the API key is bad.
mohit: Repro steps I used to hit it: 
1) Install Little Snitch + enable network extension
2) Run the Swift quickstart from Xcode (sample app)
3) Click "Run first call" -> app logs connection reset error
4) Run `curl -v https://api.play.redwood.ai/v1/health -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY"` -> returns billing_required JSON
5) Disable the network extension -> sample app shows the billing_required JSON too (so the real issue is billing gating), but the original connection reset hides that.
fiona: Oh nice repro. So it's a usability problem: local interceptors mask the real server response. People open an issue about tls or their key when the underlying cause is org billing.
grace: Action items: 1) Quickstart README: add a short "macOS network extensions / VPN" troubleshooting bullet recommending disabling app-level network filters for first-call; 2) SDK change: when transport errors occur in platform-specific frameworks (NSURLSession), capture and surface the underlying transport response body if available, and include a hint: "If you see a connection reset, verify local network filters and whether your org has billing setup."
ops-bot: DEVEX-1182 created "mac quickstart: network extension intercepts mask billing_required on first-call" assigned to mohit
mohit: I'll add a tiny example to the README showing `curl -v` and what the billing_required JSON looks like and a one-liner to test connectivity: `python -c "import requests; print(requests.get('https://api.play.redwood.ai/v1/health', headers={'Authorization': 'Bearer $KEY'}).text)"`
fiona: For immediate workaround I told the user to temporarily disable Little Snitch and accept the trial billing page in the org console. After that the sample app showed the normal 402 JSON and the first call succeeded with a proper error message.
grace: Also add to SDK parity board: ensure Node/Python/Swift clients treat transport-level connection resets as separate from 4xx app-level responses. Filed DEVEX-1183 to track parity work.
devex-bot: new issue created: DEVEX-1183 "sdk parity: surface transport resets vs billing/401 distinctly" assigned to eng-infra
mohit: small PR coming with docs + a short troubleshooting snippet. link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quickstart/pull/92
ops-bot: will monitor first-call failure telemetry after the PR lands to see if these disappear.
fiona: thanks team — this saved a confused customer ticket.
